Controls.Remediation: Correct the local baseline before relying on any audit result.
Install jq before running Claudit.
Install curl before running Claudit.
Declare a syntactically valid, explicitly authorized business domain.
Install a DNS resolver client such as dnsutils, or use the configured DNS-over-HTTPS collector.
Review the expected public A records and remove stale endpoints.
Review the expected public IPv6 records and remove stale endpoints.
Publish the intended MX route or an explicit null MX for domains that do not receive mail.
Maintain authoritative name servers with a reviewed provider and redundancy.
Review public TXT records and remove obsolete verification tokens.
Publish CAA records limiting issuance to approved certificate authorities.
Publish DMARC with an enforcement policy and monitored aggregate reporting.
Publish one SPF record, keep DNS lookup mechanisms within the RFC limit, and authorize only active senders.
Enable DNSSEC with the registrar and validate delegation at independent resolvers.
Publish an MTA-STS TXT policy when this domain receives business email.
Publish TLS-RPT to receive failed TLS delivery reports.
Publish at least one configured DKIM selector for every authorized outbound mail platform.
Review the bounded configured subdomain inventory and investigate names whose DNS evidence is unavailable.
Install the configured dnsx binary or disable optional dnsx discovery; keep the wordlist, resolver and rate limits bounded.
Set desired RRset TTLs within the approved minimum and maximum, then verify through the configured resolver.
Investigate resolver divergence, split-horizon intent or incomplete propagation before approving a DNS change.
Fix the TLS listener, certificate chain or expiry before using this domain for business traffic.
Install AWS CLI v2 and use an authorized read-only profile.
Restore read-only account access and verify the selected profile and region.
Enable a multi-region CloudTrail with protected centralized retention.
Enable hardware or virtual MFA for the AWS account root user.
Configure the IAM password policy to meet minimum length, maximum age and reuse-prevention requirements.
Disable and replace active IAM user access keys older than the configured maximum age.
Enable multi-region CloudTrail and log-file validation on a retained trail.
Remove public administrative security-group ingress; retain only explicitly approved public ports.
Enable an active, successfully delivering VPC Flow Log for every in-scope VPC.
Install Azure CLI and authenticate with a read-only subscription role.
Restore read-only subscription access and verify the selected subscription.
Configure and test activity-log alerts for high-impact control-plane events.
Review privileged role assignments and allow only explicitly approved principal object IDs.
Remove high-risk Microsoft Graph application roles from service principals or approve a narrowly scoped exception outside Claudit.
Set each storage account network default action to Deny and approve only required private or firewall paths.
Enable purge protection on every in-scope Key Vault.
Install gcloud and authenticate with a read-only project role.
Restore read-only project access and verify the selected project.
Move the project into the approved organization or update the baseline after an authorized scope review.
Create a user-managed central logging sink with protected retention.
Remove primitive IAM roles or allow only explicitly approved members while migrating to least-privilege roles.
Configure allServices audit logging for every log type required by the baseline.
Disable and replace user-managed service-account keys older than the configured maximum age.
Enable OS Login in project common instance metadata and validate required exceptions separately.
Provide a short-lived read-only API token outside the repository and verify tailnet scope.
Remove, investigate or reauthorize devices that exceed the approved last-seen threshold.
Expire long-lived, reusable or preauthorized auth keys and replace them with narrowly scoped short-lived credentials.
Replace universal allow rules with least-privilege ACLs or grants and validate the policy before deployment.
Use a least-privilege Microsoft Graph token and confirm tenant read access.
Restrict self-service email subscriptions in the tenant authorization policy.
Validate Conditional Access coverage for all users, privileged roles, applications and exclusions.
Enable Security Defaults or require MFA or an approved authentication strength for privileged directory roles.
Enable Security Defaults or block Exchange ActiveSync and other legacy clients for all users with Conditional Access.
Reduce permanent Global Administrator assignments to the configured maximum and use eligible time-bound roles where available.
Restrict guest invitations to the roles permitted by the tenant baseline.
Restrict default users from registering applications unless the baseline explicitly permits it.
Remove default-user permission grant policies or constrain consent according to the approved baseline.
Reduce tenant sharing to the approved baseline and review existing external links.
Disable legacy authentication protocols unless an approved exception exists.
Require the accepting identity to match the invited guest.
Restrict OneDrive synchronization from unmanaged devices.
Block risky file extensions from the sync client according to policy.
Set deleted-user OneDrive retention at or above the approved baseline.
Grant only the Graph read scope necessary to assess OneDrive.
Restore the isolated read-only Exchange collector and its least-privilege access.
Enforce the approved Exchange authentication baseline.
Enable and retain the required Exchange audit evidence.
Disable unintended SMTP client authentication.
Disable POP3 unless an approved exception exists.
Disable IMAP4 unless an approved exception exists.
Block external automatic forwarding by default.
Enable DKIM for every business mail domain.
Enable unified Exchange audit logging.
Review mailbox forwarding rules and exceptions.
Review transport rules and external delivery controls.
Review tenant and mailbox authentication exceptions.
Restore AWS inventory collection before treating downstream posture as complete.
Restore Azure inventory collection before treating downstream posture as complete.
Restore GCP inventory collection before treating downstream posture as complete.
Declare one explicitly authorized VPS target.
Install OpenSSH client before running host checks.
Restore read-only SSH access using an existing approved identity.
Stop unexpected wildcard listeners or add only reviewed business ports to the baseline allow-list.
Apply tested security and package updates until pending updates are within the approved threshold.
Enable and verify a supported host firewall with least-privilege inbound rules.
Enable persistent authentication logging and grant the audit identity read access to evidence.
Set PasswordAuthentication no in the effective SSH daemon configuration and validate access before reload.
Set PermitRootLogin no in the effective SSH daemon configuration and use an approved administrative identity.
Review the declared SSH exposure and firewall policy.
Review desired and observed DNS RRsets in the change plan; approve changes in the provider console and reassess.
